alt: The six stages of the accounting cycle in order: a transaction, its source document, the subsidiary book, the ledger, the trial balance and the financial statements, after which balances are carried forward and the cycle repeats.
caption: Figure: the six stages of the accounting cycle

alt: Tendai's Tuck Shop on 28 December: assets of US$5,600 (bank 4,000, shop fittings 800, inventory 800) equal capital of 3,100 plus a loan of 2,000 and trade payables of 500, which also total US$5,600.
caption: Figure: assets equal capital plus liabilities at 28 December

alt: Chipo's bank account in May: starting from 2,350, receipts of 1,180, 640 and 935 and payments of 860, 420, 275 and 300 in date order leave a closing balance of US$3,250, the balance carried down and brought down on the debit side.
caption: Figure: the bank balance moves from 2,350 to 3,250 through May

alt: Tatenda's bank reconciliation: the updated cash book balance of US$2,777 plus unpresented cheques of 1,468 (412 and 1,056) less the uncredited deposit of 930 equals the bank statement balance of US$3,315.
caption: Figure: reconciling the cash book balance of 2,777 to the bank statement balance of 3,315

alt: Tendai's capital: US$22,000 at 1 January plus profit of 6,750 less drawings of 7,200 gives US$21,550 at 31 December, so capital fell by 450 because he drew out more than he earned.
caption: Figure: capital rises with profit and falls with drawings

alt: Income statement for Tendai's Hardware: revenue of US$48,600 less cost of sales of 30,300 (opening inventory 4,200 plus purchases 31,250 less closing inventory 5,150) gives gross profit of 18,300; wages 6,800, rent 3,600 and electricity 1,150 leave a profit for the year of 6,750.
caption: Figure: closing the accounts to the income statement gives a profit of 6,750

alt: The rule of debit and credit on a T account: debit entries increase assets, expenses and drawings and decrease liabilities, capital and income; credit entries increase liabilities, capital and income and decrease assets, expenses and drawings.
caption: Figure: which side of a T account increases each type of account

alt: Reducing-balance depreciation of Rudo's van at 25%: cost of US$24,000 gives charges of 6,000, 4,500 and 3,375, so accumulated depreciation rises to 6,000, 10,500 and 13,875 while net book value falls to 18,000, 13,500 and 10,125, with smaller falls each year.
caption: Figure: the van's depreciation charge shrinks each year under the reducing-balance method

alt: Straight-line depreciation of Farai's cutting machine: cost of US$18,000 is split each year between accumulated depreciation, growing by 4,000 a year to 16,000, and net book value, falling from 14,000 to 10,000, 6,000 and finally the residual value of 2,000.
caption: Figure: each year 4,000 of the machine's cost moves from net book value to accumulated depreciation

alt: The ledger is divided into three parts: the sales ledger holds each credit customer's account (normally a debit balance), the purchases ledger holds each credit supplier's account (normally a credit balance), and the general ledger holds all other accounts; all are posted from the books of prime entry.
caption: Figure: the three divisions of the ledger

alt: Appropriation of T and N Transport's profit of US$31,620: add interest on drawings of 600, deduct interest on capital of 3,900 and Nyasha's salary of 4,800, leaving residual profit of 23,520, shared 3 to 2 as 14,112 for Tatenda and 9,408 for Nyasha.
caption: Figure: from profit of 31,620 to the partners' shares of the residual profit

alt: Thandeka's purchases ledger control account for December: the amount owed to suppliers of US$5,380 rises with credit purchases of 22,640 and falls with payments of 20,155, discount received of 497 and returns outwards of 865, leaving US$6,503 owed.
caption: Figure: how the amount owed to suppliers moves from 5,380 to 6,503

alt: Rent receivable for 2025: Nyasha received US$6,600 and December's rent of 600 was still owing, so rent earned for the year is US$7,200 (12 months at 600), and the accrued 600 is an asset at 31 December.
caption: Figure: rent earned is the cash received plus the accrued income

alt: Nyasha's sales ledger control account for December: trade receivables of US$6,240 rise with credit sales of 18,750 and a dishonoured cheque of 345, and fall with receipts of 16,385, discount allowed 412, returns inwards 638 and irrecoverable debts 290, leaving US$7,610.
caption: Figure: how the sales ledger control account moves from 6,240 to 7,610
